Junior Industrial Designer
Simulands is a company specialized in developing Human Grade simulators for training, research, and education in the cardiovascular field. Our solutions enable physicians and professionals to practice with real devices supported by real imaging, replicating complex clinical conditions in a safe and controlled environment.
Our mission is to transform the way cardiology is taught and learned, making clinical practice safer for patients and more effective for physicians. By combining engineering, research, and passion, we create learning experiences that go beyond theory, preparing the cardiologists of the future with concrete, realistic, and innovative tools.
We are looking for a Junior Industrial Designer to join our design team. The ideal candidate has a strong passion for design, technical curiosity, and a desire to grow in a collaborative and dynamic environment.
Function: Junior Industrial Designer
Job Type: Full Time position
Reporting to: Design Manager
Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Industrial Design or related fields
Languages: Fluent English oral \& written. German represents a plus.
Personal traits: We are looking for someone with a structured and disciplined approach to work, coupled with strong attention to detail. The ideal candidate is eager to learn, proactive in tackling challenges independently, and capable of managing their responsibilities with minimal supervision. Success in this role requires adaptability to shifting priorities, the ability to stay organized, and a collaborative spirit to contribute effectively within a small, fast\-paced Design team.

Highly skilled in 3D CAD applications (SolidWorks)
Experienced in continuous CAD surfacing theory.
Knowledge of other modelling software (Rhino, Blender, etc...)
Knowledge in 2D design software (Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, In Design, etc)
Experienced in rendering software (Keyshot)
Ability to create prototypes with rapid prototyping tools
Familiarity with 3D printing technologies: FDM, SLA, MultiJet/PolyJet, and SLS
Understanding of traditional manufacturing processes (molding, machining, composite materials, etc.)
Strong attention to detail, aesthetic sensibility, and technical accuracy.
Team player attitude, proactivity, and willingness to learn
Basic skills in UX/UI and design thinking processes (nice to have)
Familiarity with Figma for prototyping and digital interface support (nice to have)

Involvement in full design process from initial design concept through to final product launch.
Support the team in product and component design, from concept to prototype
Create sketches, 3D models, and high\-quality renderings
Collaborate with engineering and production departments to turn concepts into feasible solutions
Contribute to research on materials, design trends, and innovation
Prepare presentations and technical documentation for projects and clients
Take ownership of projects and capability of working without close supervision
Interested?
Please attach your CV and portfolio (PDF), highlighting your design projects and 3D modeling experience. We look forward to discovering your creativity and skills!

### Packaging Project Developer (H/F) - Conception et industrialisation ###

Véritable chef·fe d-orchestre des projets packaging, vous assurez le suivi complet des mandats, de la prise de brief jusqu-à la livraison finale, y compris la conception intégrable des emballages et le développement technique des tracés. A ce titre, vous :
* Développez des emballages sur mesure, de l-idée initiale à la validation industrielle : de l-étui simple aux concepts les plus complexes, en passant par les boîtes montées, coffrets et solutions d-expédition.
* Traduisez les besoins clients en solutions structurelles performantes
* Développez et optimisez les tracés de découpe (plans 2D / volumes 3D) en tenant compte des contraintes matériaux et production
* Réalisez les maquettes et prototypes à l-aide de nos outils internes (table de découpe, laser, collage, montage, finitions)
* Planifiez les étapes du projet (délais, coûts, qualité) en contact direct avec les clients, nos équipes de production et partenaires externes
* Accompagnez la mise en production et assurez la cohérence technique jusqu-au produit final
Note importante : ce poste ne s-adresse pas aux graphistes ou spécialistes du prépresse, il est exclusivement orienté vers le développement technique de l-emballage.

* Formation de technologue en emballage, spécialiste packaging, formation équivalente ou supérieure
* Expérience confirmée dans la conception technique d-emballages
* Maîtrise des outils de conception packaging (ArtiosCAD)
* Très bonnes connaissances des matériaux (carton compact, ondulé, supports spéciaux), procédés d-impression et de transformation
* Esprit analytique et créatif, orienté solutions
* Autonomie, précision et sens des responsabilités
* Très bonne maîtrise du français et de l-anglais (obligatoire)

Your tasks
Shape the hardware identity: Define how our humanoids look and feel: proportions, surfaces, overall silhouette. You take the design direction we already have and carry it through to physical systems that actually ship.
Design for passive safety first: Safety sits in the geometry from the first sketch. You work through clearances, pinch points, contact surfaces and fall behavior so the robot is safe around people before software gets involved.
Integrate complex systems: Package the internals (sensors, cameras, cooling, connectors, cable routing) so the technical parts look intended.
Physical human machine interaction: Design status signals, touchpoints and small physical cues that tell the people working next to the robot what it is doing and what comes next.
Build the ecosystem around the robot: Extend the design language to charging docks, transport cases, maintenance gear and packaging.
From model to CAD: You build physical models fast, see what holds up, and change them until they do. Then you do the surfacing and hand over CAD that engineering can build from directly.
Materials and processes: Select finishes, review physical samples, and work suppliers on feasibility, cost and lead times. You are willing to try materials that are not standard and to bring in specialized external labs.
Your profile
Background: A degree in industrial or product design, or an engineering degree where the design side is clearly the stronger half.
Experience: Around five years or more designing physical products, in house or at a studio. Robotics, medical devices, lab and industrial equipment, mobility, or another field where the hardware has to hold up in front of people.
Small series: You have worked on products built in the hundreds rather than the millions, and know how much that changes what a shape can be.
Safety and regulation: You have designed under mechanical safety requirements before, so guarding, clearances and contact safety are familiar territory rather than a new topic.
Tools: Surface modeling in Rhino, Onshape, SolidWorks or Fusion, plus 3D printing and enough workshop practice to build your own models.
Working with engineers: You read mechanical drawings, keep up in technical discussions, and can explain why a design decision matters.
Languages: Fluent English. German is nice to have, not a requirement.
Why us?
Ownership from day one: The physical design and hardware identity of our humanoids is yours. Short decisions, no approval chains, and you work directly with the founders and lead engineers.
Everything under one roof: Labs, workshop and test rigs are in the same Kreuzberg building. The engineer you need is a walk away, not a ticket.
Room to get better: Paid learning time and a personal budget for it, projects where something is allowed to not work the first time, and support for portfolio work and conference talks as the company becomes known.
Benefits: A benefits package you put together yourself, covering mobility, home setup, health or food. Plus one extra paid day off a year for volunteering or a project you care about.

Send us your portfolio and a few lines about one product you took from sketch to production : what changed along the way, and why. No cover letter needed.
Process : Intro call -> Portfolio deep-dive with the founders -> Half-day on-site visit with a small design exercise -> Offer.
We build robots for everyone, so we want a team that reflects that. We hire on what you can do, and we welcome applications from people who are underrepresented in hardware design. If you don't tick every box but think this is your job, apply anyway.
